O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ("M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap") and the 90 anchor ("every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts"), closer to 90.
O1.justification: 101 of the 119 frozen assertions passed under my independent execution (M1 13/13, M2 27/27, M3 15/15, M4 12/12, M5 12/12, M6 6/13, M7 0/9, M8 16/18). Seven of the eight in-scope milestones are green on the instrument's own bar — coverage-validated suite plus a passing web choreography segment — which is well past the 60 anchor. It stops short of 90 on two counts the 90 anchor names explicitly. First, the platform-proof artifacts do not exist at all: ios-simulator-m6 and ios-simulator-m8 are both recorded status "not-recorded"/pass:null, so m6-a01..a07 and m8-a17/a18 (9 assertions) have no admissible evidence. Second, M7 was never attempted (ENVIRONMENT.md defers it), and applicability.json keeps its 9 assertions in the denominator as not-passed regardless of status. Quality of the passes is high rather than nominal: every M1-M5 assertion was re-derived through the custom-client API, raw HTTP or browser automation, several with stronger methods than the suite uses (a real 65 s wait for the edit window instead of the dev clock seam; a persistent on-disk replica for the expiry purge).

O2.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ("a few medium defects off the happy path") and the 90 anchor ("only cosmetic nits").
O2.justification: Nothing I executed below the scale envelope misbehaved: zero failed assertions across M1-M5, M6-web and M8-web, no crash, no wrong data, and 58 lines of backend log with no error or exception during the whole grading session. The two major defects (d-01, d-02) are both confined to the 1,000-user / 100k-message envelope and are the lane's own recorded probe failures, consistent with run-record performance.gatePassed=false — a send/render stall past 30 s in the 50-member busy group, and a cold offline acquisition that never completes for the ~1000-conversation account. Those are worse than "medium", which holds the score below the midpoint of the interval; that they are unreachable in ordinary use, and that the remaining findings are two minors and two cosmetics, holds it well above 60. Note on double counting: the missing native simulator artifact is not filed as a defect here because it is a checklist gap, and it is scored where it belongs, in O1 and O4.

O3.anchorsCited: At the 90 anchor ("every probe correctly denied, including asset access after view-once/delete"), discounted slightly for narrower coverage than a rotated wave set.
O3.justification: DEVIATION: no holdout probe set was hash-committed for this wave, so O3 could not be scored on its frozen basis. Rather than invent probes or leave an applicable dimension unscored, I wrote nine trust-boundary probes covering every category the brief publishes and ran them alongside the eight trust-boundary checklist assertions; all results are in grading/results-trust.json and are reported here, not in probeResults, because they are not the wave's rotated set. Every boundary held server-side rather than by UI absence: a non-member's history/apiHistory/message/searchIn/roster on someone else's DM leaked nothing; the private chat photo was refused to a non-member (404) and unauthenticated (401); after removal the server served no post-removal message to the removed member and refused her writes (NOT_MEMBER); ordinary logout revoked only its own session family while logout-all killed an independently issued session, matching API.md; the replica-only held queries were refused (E_QUERY_HELD) instead of silently answered; non-member send/react/seen and foreign edit/delete were refused (NOT_MEMBER, NOT_AUTHOR); non-admin promote/rename/add were refused (NOT_ADMIN); the view-once asset returned 410 E_ASSET_VIEWED on the second fetch per principal and 416 on a Range request; a deleted message's asset returned 404 E_ASSET_UNKNOWN; an edit after the shortened window was refused EDIT_WINDOW_CLOSED on real elapsed time; and the scheduled digest counted zero from a chat the target was not a member of and zero from a group after his membership ended, while a genuine member of both counted 2. Held below 90 only because my substitute set is narrower than a rotated wave set — in particular the published "server-side denials surviving the offline cache" category could only be exercised in the browser replica, since the native artifact that category leans on does not exist.

O4.anchorsCited: At the 30 anchor ("cold-start offline shows an empty or broken app"); the 60 anchor ("reads work; offline writes lost or mis-ordered, or receipts wrong after flush") presumes a working native cold-start read path that was never demonstrated.
O4.justification: O4's designated basis under applicability.json is the harness's mechanically checkable simulator choreography artifacts, never builder assertions. That basis is empty. Both segment summaries record supplementalExternal status "not-recorded" with pass:null (ios-simulator-m6, ios-simulator-m8), and choreography/simulator.md — which requires a bound m6-ios-screen.mp4, m6-ios-receipts.jsonl and m6-ios-run.json and states that "O4/native scoring remains null or failed until this artifact exists" — has no counterpart anywhere in the lane; artifacts/m*-ios/ contain only exported Expo/Hermes bundles. So no native cold-start offline behaviour, durable-queue restart or multi-device convergence was demonstrated at all, which is at least as weak as the 30 anchor. Two things keep it from going below 30. The dimension explicitly weighs "honesty of any gap between claim and guarantee", and this lane is exemplary there: it records pass:null with an explanatory reason, copies nothing into a native pass, and its run-record notes say the native evidence is unavailable rather than claiming it. And the harness's own web segments do mechanically demonstrate real offline behaviour in the browser — offline-message-queue-flush-in-order (flushMs 8802), warm-offline-search-over-synced-messages, disappearing-message-expiry-and-purge (315 s), and M8's dual-offline convergence (firstFlushMs 13556, secondFlushMs 20338.5) and receipts reaching read — which is evidence of the same product behaviour even though it is not the simulator proof the anchors describe. Applicability forbids null here because M6 is green, so 30 is the honest placement.

O5.bandRationale: First-match evaluation in the frozen order 0, 30, 60, 90, 75 stops at 30. Band 0 does not fire: the invariant manifest conformed at every checkpoint and at the full corpus (evidence/replay-full-verification.json manifest:true, pass:true, 1008 users / 50228 posts / 100015 messages / busy chat 10000, with the named O5 fixtures u0500, u0005, u0900, u0901 and g0001 all checked exactly), and the replay finished in 2396.1 s wall (2323.2 s execution, 72.9 s checkpoint-excluded, 167243 actions settled) without exhausting its cap. Band 30 then fires on both of its disjuncts. A degradation rule fails: the M8 Insights mid-curve predicate, with the 50% checkpoint p95 at 1.8170 ms against a 1.8092 ms interpolated limit (evidence/scale-degradation.json, midCurvePass:false). And probes error or time out: the 50-member-group receipt/send-render probe produced 0 of 20 samples and failed on "sent message settled within 30 seconds" after earlier observations of 38.6 s and 42.4 s send/render (evidence/scale-receipt-render.json and siblings), and the central 1000-conversation offline-acquisition probe timed out at 90 s with no samples (evidence/scale-central-1000-acquisition.json). The lane's own run record agrees the gate did not pass (socialMessenger.performance.gatePassed=false). Every other frozen rule passed with margin: deep paging 1.09-1.24x, following fan-out 0.99-1.35x, celebrity read path 0.93-1.17x, celebrity write path 1.19x (44.7 ms vs 53.2 ms p95 for a 5-follower vs 900-follower author), global search 0.58x and Trending 1.61x, all against a 3x limit. Per the brief this is a scale-safety gate; absolute latencies here are diagnostics only and no cross-backend speed claim is implied. DEVIATION: with no rotated probe set committed, these are the lane's recorded probe measurements read from receipts, not grader-executed rotated probes.
